components.gap: Not covered on the input route. The entry gives the general normal-form theorem (systematic-power.tex lines 61-84, annex lines 10-65) but the route does not supply the source's worked normal forms and their boundary (Hempel-Oppenheim 1948, pp. 166, 168-169): (a) the L1 computations: the four minimal sentences and the four maximal sentences of L1 (one constant a, unary P and Q), the minimal normal forms of P(a) and Q(a), the maximal normal forms of P(a) and of P(a) -> Q(a), the vacuous-conjunction and four-minimal-sentence forms of a formally true and a formally false sentence, and the counts m_U = 2, 1, 0, 4 with l_U = m - m_U for those examples; (b) the L2 example: a second constant b and a binary predicate R give eight atomic sentences and 256 minimal sentences, the source's sample minimal sentence, and minimal normal forms of P(a) and Q(a) with 128 conjoined minimal sentences each; (c) the boundary that a minimal sentence does have consequences other than itself that are not formally true, none of them of singular form, with the source's witness (Ex)(P(x) v Q(x)) of P(a) v Q(a); the entry's restriction to singular consequences presupposes this but never states or demonstrates it; (d) the source's statements that a maximal sentence is the dual of a minimal sentence (n. 36), that the minimal normal form indicates content and the maximal normal form indicates range, the variety of possible states of the world that would make the sentence true, each maximal sentence describing one such state as completely as L allows, and that range and content vary inversely (the entry has only the bare counting identity). On the route these items appear only as a forward reference (inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02b-p15-025.tex lines 18-24 and 374-376) to labels defined in the unrouted handbook/parts/p15/inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02c-p15-028.tex (and, for (d), in the unrouted handbook/parts/p15/inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02c-p15-029.tex, section 'Content, range and the duality of the two normal forms'); no file on the handbook input route (handbook/main.tex -> parts/p15.tex, annex/p15.tex) inputs it, so it is not credited.

components.gap: Not covered on the input route. Definition (8.1) itself is supplied (systematic-power.tex lines 89-108), but the route omits the source's justification and data construal for it (Hempel-Oppenheim 1948, pp. 164-165 and n. 33): (a) the intuitive characterization that the systematic power of T is reflected in the ratio of the amount of information derivable by means of T to the amount of initial information the derivation requires, relativized to the data because that ratio depends on them, with the comparison of theories that derive many data from little initial information against theories that need more initial data or yield fewer results; (b) the step that obtains values between 0 and 1 inclusive by taking the percentage of the data derivable from the remainder by means of T, the form that (8.1) then applies to minimal sentences; (c) the convention that every singular sentence of L expresses a potential datum, with note 33: 'datum' covers actual as well as potential data, the convention is plausible especially if the primitive predicates refer to directly observable attributes, and that observability assumption is not essential for the definition and formal theory of sections 8 and 9 (a remark that removes a hypothesis). Text for these exists only in the unrouted handbook/parts/p15/inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02c-p15-029.tex, section 'What the measure explicates, and what counts as a datum'; no file on the handbook input route (handbook/main.tex -> parts/p15.tex, annex/p15.tex) inputs it, so it is not credited.

components.gap: Not covered on the input route. (9.1), (9.4) and (9.5) are supplied (systematic-power.tex lines 127-137), but the route omits the source's evaluation of the uniform measure and its account of the alternative (Hempel-Oppenheim 1948, p. 170 with n. 39): (a) that Carnap showed the range measure r1 to confer on the corresponding logical probability p1 characteristics incompatible with the intended meaning of logical probability ([Inductive Logic], pp. 80-81), and that Carnap, and Helmer jointly with Hempel and Oppenheim, proposed alternative range measures leading to more satisfactory concepts of probability or degree of confirmation; (b) the source's description of Carnap's alternative: a specific weight, not the same for all maximal sentences, assigned to each maximal sentence, the range measure r2 of any other singular sentence defined as the sum of the weights of its constituent maximal sentences, and p2(T, S) = r2(T.S)/r2(S). Theorem thm:p15-power-weight-choice (lines 375-398) shows uniform weights leaving p_r(B, A) at its prior but neither reports nor attributes Carnap's objection, and lines 444-455 only name the Carnap and Helmer-Hempel-Oppenheim constructions. Text for (a)-(b) exists only in the unrouted handbook/parts/p15/inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02c-p15-029.tex, section 'The uniform measures and Carnap's objection'; no file on the handbook input route (handbook/main.tex -> parts/p15.tex, annex/p15.tex) inputs it, so it is not credited.

components.gap: Partial. The statement (systematic-power.tex lines 321-345; line 328 'The converse transformation holds as well') promises the converse half of source Theorem (9.13) (p. 173: the same exchange, with 's' replaced by 'p', transforms any theorem about s into a theorem about p), but its proof is only 'The same argument proves the converse transformation' (annex lines 528-536). The written steps owed for the converse are not given: the term identity p_r(D(B), D(C)) = s_r(B(~A_1,...,~A_m), C(~A_1,...,~A_m)), the transfer of definedness r(D(C)) = g(C(~A_1,...,~A_m)), the substitution of negated sentences into a universally valid s-statement, and the reversal of an entailment hypothesis in that direction. A converse proof exists only in the unrouted handbook/parts/p15/inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02c-p15-029.tex, section 'The converse half of the Dualism Theorem'; no file on the handbook input route (handbook/main.tex -> parts/p15.tex, annex/p15.tex) inputs it, so it is not credited.
